segments.text: Let's walk through this proof: Number of odd-degree vertices is even. The sum of all degrees is always twice the number of edges. Handshaking Lemma: every edge has two endpoints, contributing 2 to the total degree sum.
Therefore, the total sum must be even. Any integer multiplied by 2 is even.
Split the sum into even-degree and odd-degree vertices. Partitioning the set of vertices into those with even degree and those with odd degree.
The sum of even degrees is itself even. A sum of even numbers is always even.
So the sum of odd degrees must also be even. If (Even + X) is even, then X must be even.

To get an even sum, you must have an even number of odd terms. An odd number added to itself an odd number of times is odd; an odd number added to itself an even number of times is even. Thus, to get an even sum from odd numbers, you need an even number of them. Notice that a step is skipped here. Explain that if you sum k odd numbers, the sum is even if and only if k is even. So, in summary: The logic is sound, but S6 skips the final parity argument connecting the sum of odd numbers to the count of those numbers.
